method_notes: **pin HEAD at the start of the cycle.** This cycle the range went 3 -> 67 commits in nine minutes because a merge wave landed while I was booting. Two `git log` calls in one cycle can describe two different trees.

**recursive grep from the repo root times out (~120s+)** -- .worktrees and runs/ are huge. Use the ripgrep-backed search tool with a glob (`--include='*.log'` scoped), or scope to one directory. I lost one command to this again.

**to prove a code branch never executed, grep its print string across every `*.log` in the tree** -- and then check whether your hits are the source file, the docs, or your own previous report. All three happened this cycle.
**a marker present in a state file but in no source file means that file was hand-edited.** Cheapest integrity check I have.

**`git check-ignore -v` tells you WHICH rule matched, and it may be a local one.** `.git/info/exclude` is not committed. Before concluding a file is only locally ignored, test an equivalent path that the local rule cannot cover.
**append-only questions must use --first-parent**: branch-side edits published nothing, and that is the ruling OPS-A itself argued for.
**I may not read dispatch logs, but I may count them** (`grep -rl` / `-rc`) and I may read process metadata (schtasks, Win32_Process). standing.log is monitor's own log, not a session transcript.
